summary.intent: Run the Phase 43 FUSE write-durability UAT on Linux against a local stack (API, mock-ipns-router, Linux desktop) connected to a shared Docker Compose infra at 192.168.133.49.
summary.outcome: All 4 UAT tests completed on Linux/FUSE (Tests 1-3 PASS, Test 4 reproduced known gap G-43-UAT-02). A notification spam bug was found, fixed, and committed. A stale-mount-after-crash finding was logged as a GSD todo. The push to remote was in progress at session end.

repo: Cargo builds go to the workspace-root target/ (e.g. /home/michael/Code/cipher-box/target/debug/), NOT the crate-local apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/debug/. A stale Feb 28 binary in the crate-local path caused a multi-hour phantom deadlock investigation.

Debug builds load devUrl (http://localhost:1420) via Tauri config — the vite dev server must be running for the webview to load anything. The hidden dev-key webview (visible:false) will silently fail to run auth JS without it.

WebKitGTK in headless/no-GPU Linux environments requires: WEBKIT_DISABLE_SANDBOX_THIS_IS_DANGEROUS=1 (bwrap can't map uid without user namespaces), LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 + MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3 (no Vulkan/Zink), and setsid for proper process group handling.

Journal entries are intentionally retained on disk after a successful runtime upload (not removed until next mount replay) — this is design decision CR-08. Normal-seeming 'Pending' entries post-upload are expected.

test-login (test-auth.service.ts) does NOT provision a vault. The client must create it during onboarding. A user with is_new=false but no IPNS record (e.g. stale uninitialized vault in shared Postgres) will hang resolving a never-published record.
The shared Postgres at 192.168.133.49 had a stale dev-key@cipherbox.local user with initialized_at=null and 21 orphaned pins from a prior partial run. Deleting the user cascades vault + pins cleanly.
SyncStatus::WriteParked is emitted by the SDK daemon on every 30s poll while any Failed entry exists — it is level-triggered by design. The desktop callback must edge-trigger notifications itself.
The cipherbox-desktop binary's feature flag defaults to 'fuse' (libfuse3) on Linux — no explicit flag needed for the correct FUSE build.

code.finding: Stale-mount-after-crash bug: after a SIGKILL, ~/CipherBox is a disconnected FUSE mount (ENOTCONN). mount_path.exists() calls stat() which returns ENOTCONN → false. Code takes the create_dir_all branch → EEXIST → 'Failed to create mount point: File exists (os error 17)', skipping the stale-cleanup else-branch. Normal relaunches hit the else-branch and log 'Cleaned stale mount point'; only ENOTCONN state triggers the failure.

WriteParked notification was level-triggered: send_write_parked_notification fired on every sync cycle while failed > 0. Fixed by adding an AtomicU32 watermark (last_notified_failed) that only fires when failed count rises above the last-notified value, and resets to 0 on Idle/failed==0. Watermark must NOT reset on Syncing (daemon emits Syncing at start of every cycle at sdk/src/sync.rs:109).

Journal entry removal (journal.remove) only happens in the mount-time replay path, not in the runtime upload-completion handler. Successful runtime uploads leave entries as Pending on disk by design (CR-08).
Daemon emits Syncing at the start of every poll cycle before emitting WriteParked or Idle. Any edge-trigger reset placed on Syncing will re-arm the notification every cycle, recreating the spam.

initialize_vault: first log 'Publishing vault key blob' appears after local crypto ops (generate_random_bytes, HKDF, ECIES — all sync, no locks). If this log never appears, the function body is not executing at all, likely a stale binary issue.

workflow: pkill pattern matching: pkill <pattern> in the same shell as a backgrounded '... <pattern> &' will self-match and kill the shell (exit 144). Use the bracket trick [c]ipherbox-desktop or separate kill and launch into distinct Bash calls.

Verify binary freshness by checking modification time before running (ls -la target/debug/). When builds seem to have no effect, check for a stale binary in a crate-local target/ that is shadowing the workspace-root target/.
ptrace_scope=1 blocks strace/gdb attach to non-child processes. Run the binary under gdb as a child (gdb --args ./binary) to capture backtraces; strace works on child processes launched by the shell.
When a debug-build Tauri app's webview produces no output (no page load, no JS), check whether the vite dev server is running — the devUrl config makes the entire app dependent on it in debug mode.
For shared-Postgres test environments, always check for stale test users with partial state (initialized_at=null) before running UAT that provisions new vaults.
GSD capture flow: /gsd:capture (no flag) routes to add-todo workflow, writes to .planning/todos/pending/, updates STATE.md count, and commits via gsd tool scoped to the todo file only.

friction: Stale crate-local binary (Feb 28) in apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/debug/ shadowed the real workspace-root build. Running against it produced a phantom async deadlock investigation that consumed the majority of the session.

WebKitGTK required multiple rounds of debugging (GL failure → sandbox failure → X11 backend → llvmpipe) before finding the correct combination: WEBKIT_DISABLE_SANDBOX + LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE + setsid + vite dev server.
pkill self-match pattern caused repeated accidental shell kills throughout the session when kill and launch were in the same Bash command.

Shared Postgres had a stale dev-key@cipherbox.local user with an uninitialized vault, causing the app to hang resolving a never-published IPNS record — required manual DB cleanup via a Node script run from the api directory (pg module not resolvable from /tmp).
ptrace_scope=1 blocked strace on the live process; had to relaunch under gdb as a child to capture backtraces.
No psql client on the dev machine required routing Postgres cleanup through a Node.js script.
cargo build output confusion: the build command ran successfully but the crate-local stale binary was being invoked, making it appear the build had no effect for an extended period.
open_items: Stale-mount-after-crash recovery (Linux only): mount_filesystem needs to detect ENOTCONN on stat() and run fusermount3 -u before attempting to mount, or fall through EEXIST to the stale-cleanup path. Logged as GSD todo (2026-06-14-recover-stale-fuse-mount-after-crash-on-linux-startup.md, area: desktop-fuse).
G-43-UAT-02 (carried over from Windows): filename and size fields are plaintext in cb-journal/*.json entries. Content/keys/IV are encrypted but metadata is not.
The 'mount failed' OS notification copy is non-actionable — user has no in-app recovery path and must manually run fusermount3 -u ~/CipherBox. Should be addressed alongside the stale-mount fix.
Push to remote (feat/fuse-write-durability) was requested at session end but the transcript ends at the commit step — verify the push completed.

The notification spam fix AtomicU32 watermark resets on Idle/failed==0 but does not account for a subset of parked entries being resolved while others remain — consider tracking failed IDs rather than count if partial-clear behavior matters.
